newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai no challenge to HK without convertibility.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai no challenge to HK without convertibility.

text.p: Shanghai cannot challenge Hong Kong's position as an international financial centre until the Chinese yuan becomes freely convertible, a senior Bank of China official said on Wednesday.

Zheng Bolin, deputy chief of the Bank of China's Hong Kong-Macau management office, told a seminar the fear of Shanghai replacing Hong Kong as a financial centre was understandable but was unjustified.

"Shanghai at this point is a long way behind Hong Kong in many areas. I believe that in the short term, at least before the renminbi (Chinese yuan) becomes freely convertible, Shanghai cannot become an international financial centre," Zheng said.
But he said that by the time Shanghai was ready, "the huge scale of the Chinese economy will be perfectly capable of supporting two financial centres."
"By that time, Hong Kong will still have its own advantages. Both cities will have their special characteristics, the question of one replacing the other does not exist," he added.
Zheng was speaking at a seminar on Hong Kong-China economic relations, organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council.
